lead.headline: Bitget's $388M Breach Exposes Persistent Custody Risk as Institutional Capital Flows to Tokenization
lead.tldr: North Korean state actors executed the year's largest crypto theft against Bitget, draining up to $388 million through backend wallet exploits, while traditional finance and crypto infrastructure players accelerated competing tokenization bets.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the industry's unresolved security architecture collided head-on with its institutional ambitions, and the gap between them is where we place our underwriting focus.

top_signals.title: North Korea accused of plundering Bitget for $387 million in year’s biggest crypto attack
top_signals.summary: North Korean hackers are accused of stealing $387 million from Bitget in the largest crypto attack of the year. The attackers exploited a flaw in the wallet backend to make fraudulent withdrawals appear legitimate.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The scale and sophistication of the Bitget breach—exploiting wallet backend logic rather than smart contract vulnerabilities—signals that exchange custody infrastructure remains critically exposed even at mature platforms, repricing our risk models for centralized exchange exposure.

top_signals.title: Bitget clarifies $388M in assets affected by security breach
top_signals.summary: Bitget has clarified that a security breach affected approximately $388 million in crypto assets. This event is noted as one of the largest industry hacks since the Bybit incident in 2025.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bitget's own confirmation of ~$388 million in affected assets establishes this as a defining data point for 2025 security benchmarking and will pressure remaining exchanges to disclose proof-of-reserves methodologies.

top_signals.title: Bitget crypto exchange hit by $350mn hack
top_signals.summary: Bitget crypto exchange has reported a massive security breach resulting in a $350 million loss. The company indicated that the attack patterns are highly consistent with those used by North Korean state-sponsored hackers.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Attribution to North Korean state-sponsored actors with 'highly consistent' attack patterns means this is not a novel threat vector but a persistent, well-resourced adversary that the industry has failed to price into operational security costs.

top_signals.title: KelpDAO sues LayerZero, CEO over $292M rsETH bridge exploit
top_signals.summary: KelpDAO has filed a lawsuit against LayerZero and its CEO following a massive $292 million rsETH bridge exploit. The lawsuit alleges that security failures within LayerZero's infrastructure contributed to the loss of funds.
top_signals.why_it_matters: KelpDAO's litigation against LayerZero shifts exploit liability questions from protocol governance to legal precedent, creating execution risk for bridge infrastructure valuations that underwriters can no longer ignore.

top_signals.title: Bitget confirms $351M security breach, suspends withdrawals7m
top_signals.summary: Bitget has confirmed a security breach resulting in a loss of $351 million. In response to the incident, the exchange has suspended all user withdrawals.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The suspension of all withdrawals following confirmation of a $351 million loss demonstrates that even second-tier exchanges remain operationally fragile under stress, with user fund accessibility serving as the first casualty.

top_signals.title: Crypto Biz: Wall Street and crypto fight for the same turf
top_signals.summary: Major financial institutions and crypto firms are converging on tokenization, with the NYSE and Blockchain.com collaborating on tokenized stocks. Additionally, Binance has made a significant investment in Circle while Canadian banks explore tokenized deposits.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The NYSE-Blockchain.com collaboration and Binance's Circle investment reveal that tokenization is becoming the contested terrain where traditional finance and crypto-native firms compete for identical institutional clients, compressing first-mover advantages.

deals.summary: HIFI has secured $37 million in Series A funding led by Left Lane Capital. The capital will be used to scale its infrastructure for stablecoin payments and tokenized capital markets.

HIFI has raised $37 million in a Series A funding round to scale its tokenized capital markets infrastructure. The company has already established key industry ties through collaborations with DTCC and Visa.

MoonPay is acquiring the brokerage firm North Capital for $60 million to expand its capabilities in tokenized securities. The acquisition provides MoonPay with essential licenses to accelerate its growth in the asset tokenization space.
CoinMarketCap has acquired the crypto derivatives data platform CoinGlass to expand its data offerings. CoinGlass will continue to operate under its own brand, team, and pricing structure.
Connect Ventures has raised $55 million in the first close of its fifth fund. The fund is specifically targeting deeptech founders.

on_the_radar.title: US seizes bank accounts of payments group working for Tether’s and Bitfinex’s bank
on_the_radar.summary: US prosecutors have seized the bank accounts of Capstone, a payments group accused of illegally moving hundreds of millions of dollars for Tether and Bitfinex. The operation was allegedly conducted under the direction of a Caribbean bank to bypass financial regulations.

on_the_radar.title: Fed proposes new capital, redemption rules for stablecoin issuers40m, Fed proposes new capital, redemption rules for stablecoin issuersThe Fed’s proposal would set capital requirements, a two-day redemption window and new reserve disclosures as regulators implement the GENIUS Act.
on_the_radar.summary: The Federal Reserve has proposed new regulatory requirements for stablecoin issuers, focusing on capital reserves and redemption timelines. These rules are being implemented as part of the GENIUS Act to ensure financial stability and transparency.

on_the_radar.title: More than $170 million in crypto moves from Bitget wallets to unidentified address
on_the_radar.summary: Over $170 million in cryptocurrency has been moved from Bitget wallets to an unidentified address. The exchange has not yet confirmed if this movement is the result of a security breach.

on_the_radar.title: ARK Invest brings $1.3 billion venture fund onchain through Securitize
on_the_radar.summary: ARK Invest has moved a $1.3 billion venture fund onchain via the Securitize platform. This move represents a significant expansion of their existing strategic partnership to leverage blockchain for asset management.

on_the_radar.title: US weighs overseas push for dollar-backed stablecoins: Bloomberg
on_the_radar.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly exploring strategies to promote the global adoption of dollar-backed stablecoins. This move is intended to reinforce the US dollar's global dominance and increase demand for US Treasuries.

on_the_radar.title: ECB to put its own money into tokenized securities via new Pontes DLT
on_the_radar.summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) intends to invest a portion of its funds into tokenized public-sector securities. These transactions will be settled using the new Pontes DLT infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: Manhattan US Attorney leading probe into Binance’s Iran compliance: Bloomberg
on_the_radar.summary: The Manhattan US Attorney is leading an investigation into whether Binance knowingly permitted trading that violated sanctions against Iran. This probe adds new details to an existing Department of Justice investigation into the exchange's compliance practices.

on_the_radar.title: Zano rolls blockchain back a month after Gateway Address exploit
on_the_radar.summary: Zano has implemented a blockchain rollback of approximately one month to rectify a security breach. The action follows a Gateway Address exploit that allowed unauthorized ZANO and Freedom Dollar tokens to be circulated.

on_the_radar.title: 'It's really not just a blockchain anymore': Vitalik Buterin maps Ethereum's path to 2030
on_the_radar.summary: Vitalik Buterin outlined Ethereum's long-term technical roadmap leading up to 2030, emphasizing a shift beyond traditional blockchain architecture. He highlighted the upcoming Hegota upgrade as a transition point toward advanced technologies like recursive STARKs and quantum safety.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin ETFs turn positive for 2026 with $2.4 billion weekly inflow, their largest since October
on_the_radar.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a massive $2.4 billion weekly inflow, the largest since October, pushing net flows for 2026 into positive territory. Simultaneously, Ether funds recovered from previous outflows with $690 million in net inflows.

on_the_radar.title: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce to leave post on Oct. 2
on_the_radar.summary: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, known as 'Crypto Mom' for her pro-innovation stance, is set to leave her post on October 2. Her departure removes a key internal voice advocating for clearer regulatory frameworks for digital assets.

on_the_radar.title: CFTC sues Cash FX, alleges $950M crypto-linked forex scheme
on_the_radar.summary: The CFTC has filed a lawsuit against Cash FX and three individuals for allegedly operating a $950 million crypto-linked forex scheme. The action targets fraudulent activities involving digital assets and foreign exchange trading.

linkedin_post:
Three hundred eighty-eight million dollars evaporated from Bitget's backend wallets this week, and the attackers didn't need to touch a smart contract. North Korean groups exploited reconciliation logic—making fraudulent withdrawals look legitimate to internal systems. This is not a novel exploit class. It is the same operational perimeter that FTX, that countless exchanges, have failed to harden.

We keep underwriting tokenization infrastructure at premium valuations—HIFI's $37 million Series A, MoonPay's $60 million North Capital acquisition for brokerage licenses, the NYSE itself building tokenized stock rails with Blockchain.com. The capital is moving. But the custody layer these assets will eventually sit on? Bitget just proved it is still porous at scale.

The question we are asking: when institutional allocators finally arrive in size, will they tolerate the same operational security standards that retail has absorbed as table stakes? Our bet is they will not, and that compliance-grade custody infrastructure is currently mispriced relative to the tokenization front-ends capturing attention. The reallocation, when it comes, will be abrupt.

What would kill this thesis: a major institutional tokenization launch that explicitly accepts existing exchange custody without independent audit or insurance requirements. We are watching for that signal.
